title: Rust: Date and Time
description: Work with dates, times, and durations using Rust's standard library.

steps.title: Get Current Time
steps.description: Use `std::time::Instant::now()` to measure how long a computation takes. Compute sum of 1 to 1,000,000 and print the elapsed time.

verification.failureMessage: Measure and print how long the computation takes.

steps.title: Duration Math
steps.description: Use `std::time::Duration` to represent time spans. Add 2 hours, 30 minutes, and 15 seconds together into one Duration. Convert to total seconds and print.
hints: Add with `+` operator: `h2 + m30 + s15 = 9015 seconds`

steps.title: System Time (UNIX Timestamp)
steps.description: Get the current UNIX timestamp using `std::time::SystemTime::now()`. Convert to seconds since epoch and print it.
hints: This is the current UNIX timestamp.

verification.failureMessage: Print the current UNIX timestamp (seconds since epoch).

steps.title: Time Since a Date
steps.description: Calculate how many seconds have passed since `SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH` + `Duration::from_secs(1_000_000_000)` (a specific date). Print the duration.
hints: This shows the time elapsed since Sep 9, 2001.

verification.failureMessage: Print the duration since the Unix timestamp 1,000,000,000.

steps.title: Timeout Simulation
steps.description: Simulate a timeout scenario: set a deadline `Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(10)`. Loop checking `Instant::now() < deadline` and count iterations. Print the count.
hints: `let mut count = 0; while Instant::now() < deadline { count += 1; }`
This shows how many iterations fit in 10ms.
